pages.intent: cover: name the question and the status of the numbers
pages.message: US cold-chain logistics market sizing and where to play, preliminary

pages.intent: the answer first, as numbered findings
pages.message: Cold chain is an attractive, growing market; a pharma-led entry is the hypothesis to test

exhibits.reader_must_see: the five findings and the hypothesis in reading order, each with its headline figure
exhibits.comparison: none between rows: each row pairs a short finding with its evidence
exhibits.data: five short findings, each with one or two figures from the notes

forms_considered.form: rows of navy label cells beside pale blue detail cells
forms_considered.reason: chosen: the reference's own assumptions table device, so a finding reads left to right with its evidence
loses the split between the finding and its evidence

forms_considered.form: five numbered boxes in a grid
forms_considered.reason: breaks the top-down reading order of an argument

exhibits.chosen_form: rows of navy label cells beside pale blue detail cells
exhibits.why: an executive summary is read top-down; label cells give each finding a scannable head
exhibits.in_reference_look: navy cells with white text and pale blue cells as on the reference's pages 5 and 6
exhibits.marks: nothing marked: the title states the answer and the last row states the hypothesis

pages.intent: size the market and split its growth
pages.message: The market grows from about 95 to about 135 billion dollars by 2030, about 7% a year

exhibits.reader_must_see: how the 2025 market becomes the 2030 market and how much of the step comes from pharma
exhibits.comparison: the 2025 total against the 2030 total, with the growth split into non-pharma and pharma steps
exhibits.data: two totals in billion dollars and two increments that sum to the difference

forms_considered.reason: chosen: totals and the two growth steps share one dollar scale and the steps tie to the difference
the reader would subtract segment heights to see each segment's growth

forms_considered.form: line chart of the market to 2030
forms_considered.reason: only two dated points exist in the notes; intermediate years would be invented

exhibits.why: the claim is a size and a growth split; a bridge shows both without arithmetic
exhibits.in_reference_look: navy totals and the bright blue for the pharma step, bold black chart label with a unit line, source line under the plot
exhibits.marks: the pharma step in the emphasis blue with its value; a bracket over the growth steps carrying the 7% a year rate

pages.message: Pharma is 22% of today's market but 35% of growth to 2030

exhibits.reader_must_see: that the pharma share of growth is much larger than its share of today's market
exhibits.comparison: pharma and non-pharma shares of the 2025 market against their shares of 2025 to 2030 growth
exhibits.data: two compositions of 100 percent, two segments each

forms_considered.form: two 100 percent stacked columns side by side
forms_considered.reason: chosen: the pharma segment's height in each column is the comparison, read on one scale
angles across two pies are hard to compare
works, but the reference draws composition as stacked bars and the two columns read as before and after

exhibits.chosen_form: two 100 percent stacked columns side by side
exhibits.why: the claim is a share that grows; two stacked columns put the pharma segment at the same base so its height difference reads directly
exhibits.in_reference_look: navy for non-pharma and the bright blue for pharma, segment values inside the bars in white
exhibits.marks: pharma segments in the emphasis blue with their shares labelled; the drivers text beside it names biologics and GLP-1

pages.message: Revenue grows faster than warehouse capacity, which already runs at about 82% utilisation

exhibits.reader_must_see: the gap opening between revenue growth and capacity growth to 2030
exhibits.comparison: pharma revenue, total revenue and warehouse capacity, each indexed to 2025
exhibits.data: three series of six yearly index values, compounded from the stated growth rates

forms_considered.form: indexed line chart with labels at the line ends
forms_considered.reason: chosen: three growth paths on one scale and the reference names series at line ends
states the rates but not how the gap compounds by 2030
the reader would compare numbers instead of slopes

exhibits.chosen_form: indexed line chart with labels at the line ends
exhibits.why: the claim is a widening gap; lines on one index scale show the slopes diverging
exhibits.in_reference_look: thin coloured lines, light grey gridlines, series named at the right end in their own colour, no legend
exhibits.marks: capacity line in grey and named at its end; a callout states the 82% utilisation and the tight regions

pages.intent: show the cost of adding capacity
pages.message: Cold storage costs about twice ambient to build, and energy is 25 to 30% of opex

exhibits.reader_must_see: how far the cold-storage build cost range sits above the ambient cost
exhibits.comparison: the cold build cost range against the ambient build cost per square foot
exhibits.data: one range of 220 to 260 dollars and one value of 120 dollars per square foot

forms_considered.form: floating range bar against an ambient bar on one dollar axis
forms_considered.reason: chosen: the range and the single value share one scale

forms_considered.form: two columns using the cold midpoint
forms_considered.reason: hides that the cold figure is a range
loses the dollar levels a capital plan needs

exhibits.chosen_form: floating range bar against an ambient bar on one dollar axis
exhibits.why: the claim is a multiple of a cost; two bars on a dollar axis show it and keep the levels
exhibits.in_reference_look: horizontal bars as the reference draws them, navy for cold storage, grey for ambient
exhibits.marks: the cold range's upper part in the emphasis blue, the cost of each bar written beside it

pages.message: The three routes trade off capability, capital and exposure to pharma growth

exhibits.reader_must_see: what each route buys, its exposure to growth, its cost and its open question
exhibits.data: three rows by four columns of short qualitative text with figures from the notes

forms_considered.form: table with a navy label column
forms_considered.reason: chosen: qualitative criteria read across each route and down each criterion

forms_considered.form: two by two matrix of growth exposure and capital
forms_considered.reason: would place routes on axes the notes do not measure
the criteria would not line up across routes

exhibits.chosen_form: table with a navy label column
exhibits.why: the reader compares routes criterion by criterion; a table aligns them
exhibits.in_reference_look: the reference's assumptions table: navy label cells with white text, pale blue banded cells, white rules
exhibits.marks: nothing on the table: the title states the comparison and the next page gives the answer

pages.intent: give the preliminary answer and the work to confirm it
pages.message: Hypothesis: buy a regional 3PL for capability, then build pharma-grade sites near hubs

exhibits.reader_must_see: the answer to both CEO questions and the measurements that would change it
exhibits.comparison: the case for, the choice of where to play, and the open measurements side by side
exhibits.data: three short lists of qualitative points with figures from the notes

forms_considered.form: three columns under navy header bars
forms_considered.reason: chosen: the two CEO questions and the next steps read as parallel answers
mixes the answer with the work still needed
the previous page already compares routes

exhibits.chosen_form: three columns under navy header bars
exhibits.why: the reader takes the answer and the conditions on it at once
exhibits.in_reference_look: navy header cells with white text over pale blue bodies, as the reference's tables draw labels
